effortFeature.name: THE PREPARED MIND (2 EFFORT)
effortFeature.text: You can spend 2 Effort to choose one of three powerful effects. Where the Awakened Diplomat's Power of Suggestion runs on charisma and the universe's quiet cooperation, the Prepared Mind runs on the work you have already done before the scene began. - Cite the File. Declare you have read about this person, this house, this faction, or this situation in advance. The Keeper provides one true and useful fact about them, a vulnerability, a recent event, a relationship, a stated position, that you may not have learned yet but that fits what your character could reasonably have prepared. - Anticipated Move. When the next NPC in the scene takes a social or political action, you may declare that you anticipated it. You take a Reaction now, before the action resolves, to counter or complicate it, and you have Advantage on that Reaction; the Keeper sets its scope. Foresight sharpens the response; it does not guarantee it. - The Quiet Word. You speak privately to one NPC currently in the scene. Whatever you say, the NPC takes seriously, not necessarily favorably, but seriously. They consider it as a credible signal. Where this leads is between you, them, and the table. > INFLUENCE SCALES WITH THE ROLL. Success: those present, this scene. With Hope: it holds after you leave. Critical: it spreads beyond the room. With Fear: it turns on you.

classFeature.name: STANDING REPUTATION
classFeature.text: Sleeping Diplomats build influence the slow way, by being reliable, but they spend the same currency every Diplomat does: Favor Tokens. The pool, the cap, the way they are earned, and the way they are spent are identical to the Awakened Diplomat's Cultural Lens (Chapter 6), so a character who Awakens or who came up Sleeping never has to relearn how their social capital works. The path changes how you fight and rest, through Effort and Resolve; it does not change how you trade in favors. You begin each session with 2 Favor Tokens and hold a maximum of 4 (raised cumulatively by background and subclass, so a Core World Sleeping Diplomat holds up to 6). You gain 1 when you succeed on a Persuasion or Deception roll, and 1 on every long rest. You spend them through your subclass abilities, through House and Free Fleet contacts (Chapter 5), to automatically succeed on an institutional task (1 Favor), or by spending 5 at once to raise your Reputation with one faction by 1 RP (Chapter 16), bought standing that can be lost again by how you act. What "Standing Reputation" names is not a separate resource but the Sleeping Diplomat's reading of the same one: every Favor is a debt of trust earned by being dependable where it was witnessed, not by performance or spectacle. Favor Tokens are not Effort. They are the slower, longer-running currency of the Diplomat's career, the same on either path. Protocol. You always know the correct form (title, gift, taboo, precedence) for any culture in common knowledge; no roll. For isolated or unknown cultures, roll Knowledge (DC set by how removed they are) to read their norms from behavior alone. Once you know the protocol, you cannot offend by accident, only by choice.

foundation.name: Thought Tide
foundation.desc: Spend 1 Hope to allow an ally to use your Presence or Instinct modifier for one roll. Once per rest, you can spend 1 Stress to grant your entire crew a mental shield, giving them Advantage on rolls to resist fear or psychic influence for one scene.

mastery.name: Collective Consciousness
mastery.desc: Once per session, you can spend 3 Hope to merge your mind with up to 3 allies in Close range for one scene. You share senses, emotions, and thoughts, gaining Advantage on all group rolls and on Instinct rolls to detect dangers.

New Domain Paths are unlocked through Study Projects during Long Rests; higher-level study requires breadth at the previous level.

The Keeper has final say on what is plausible. Once per session, you can spend 1 Hope to upgrade this declaration to a Tier 1 piece of gear or a small quantity of valuable contraband.

specialization.desc: You have Advantage on all social rolls with port officials, dockmasters, customs agents, and the working staff of stations and waystations. You can spend 1 Hope to ensure that a routine inspection of your ship turns up nothing of interest, regardless of what you are actually carrying.

mastery.name: The Long Con
mastery.desc: Once per story arc, you can spend 3 Hope to declare that an elaborate scheme you set up months or years ago has just paid off.

mastery.desc: You hold a permanent contract that no living organization currently knows you hold. Its target is a specific named individual. The contract pays out, in full, on the day they die, by your hand or by another's, the contract does not specify. You may decide, at any point, to reveal your role.

specialization.name: The Vanishing (Reaction).
specialization.desc: Spend 1 Effort. When you would be detected, captured, or photographed, you instead are not. The Keeper resolves how, narratively. Once per scene.

mastery.name: The Erased Record (Action).
mastery.desc: Once per story arc, declare that an existing piece of evidence about your activities, a security recording, a witness statement, a written note, has been erased. The Keeper helps you decide how it was done; it is now gone.

mastery.name: The Old Captain's Favor (Action).
mastery.desc: Once per story arc, call in a major favor from a senior Free Fleet, smuggler-cartel, or House-blacklist contact. The favor is significant, a ship, a passage, a name removed from a list, and is, after this use, repaid forever.

sleepingRules.name: Scoundrel
sleepingRules.desc: Scoundrels are the rats in the walls — always listening, stealing, surviving. Charm is their lockpick. Paranoia is their armor. The crew's professional liars.

effortFeature.name: HANDS THAT KNOW (2 EFFORT)
effortFeature.text: You spend 2 Effort to choose one effect: - Cased the Joint. Declare that you, or a previous version of yourself, has worked a job like this before. Name the target of a theft, a lock, or a mark; the Keeper tells you one concrete weakness, the guard's rhythm, the make of the lock, where the camera does not reach. You do not steal it for free, but you go in prepared: you have Advantage on the roll to pull the job, and the take is cleaner for knowing the way in. - The False Face. Adopt one of your established alternate identities. NPCs who do not specifically know you under your true name accept the alternate identity for the duration of the scene. - The Backup Plan. Declare that you anticipated this exact failure. You produce a contingency item, ally, or piece of information that cleanly resolves the immediate problem. Once per scene.

classFeature.name: THE QUIET NETWORK
classFeature.text: Sneak Attack. When you have Advantage on an attack, you deal an extra 1d6 damage. This is the Scoundrel's stock in trade, the hit that lands because the target never saw you set for it, and it grows as you advance: +2d6 at Tier 2, +3d6 at Tier 3. (Catching a target who does not know where you are is the usual way to earn that Advantage, but any source of Advantage on the attack arms it.) The Network. You maintain, throughout the campaign, a personal network of contacts, fences, smugglers, old crewmates, bartenders, dock supervisors. Once per session, you may declare that you know someone in the current city, station, or region. The Keeper helps you describe the contact briefly and decides what they will and will not do. Contacts have memories; they remember favors and they remember betrayals.
